purpose: cross-program referee for the VV10 (nonlocal-correlation) term of oB97X-V, independent of PySCF's nr_nlc_vxc kernel
generator: nlcsplit/ref/orca/build_anchor_json.py (values parsed out of the .out files; every entry carries the line number and the literal line)
program: ORCA 6.0.1 RELEASE (libXC 6.2.2 build; VV10 handled by ORCA's own DFT-NL, not libXC)
basis_caveat: step_h_s22.py's BASIS defaults to '6-31g*' = 6-31G(d) on heavy atoms, NOT plain 6-31G. ORCA inputs use '6-31G*', the same thing.
quantity_printed: ORCA's 'NL Energy, E(C,NL)' line in the 'DFT components' block. ORCA 6.0.1 prints it natively for WB97X-V — no two-run subtraction was needed. The WB97X (no -V) control in ref/h2o_wb97x.out has no such line.
sign_convention_note: ORCA's E(C,NL) and PySCF's numint.nr_nlc_vxc both report the full VV10 term (double sum + beta*int rho), so the two are directly comparable in the superposition difference; the beta*int rho piece cancels exactly because the dimer electron count equals the sum of the fragment counts.
geometry: GMTKN55 S22 official geometries, scratch/lit/s22/S22_02.xyz (water) and S22_11.xyz (benzene, geometry A sandwich). Monomers are the fragments CUT AT THE COMPLEX GEOMETRY, matching step_h_s22.geomlib_sub(), not relaxed monomers. See nlcsplit/ref/orca/PROVENANCE.txt.
grid: ORCA defaults: main DFT grid Lebedev-302 max / radial OptM3-with-GC(2021); separate NL (VV10) grid Lebedev-110 max, IntAcc 4.004. PySCF side used grids.level=1. Grids are NOT matched between programs.
parallel_note: %pal nprocs>1 is BROKEN in this container: ORCA calls 'mpirun' (<cluster-home>/bin/mpirun) and it dies at Startup. All six runs here are SERIAL (%pal nprocs 1). Serial only affects cost, not the VV10 value.

audit_trail_of_rejected_claims: During this round the running agent reported four things that the files do not support; each was caught by re-reading the artifact rather than the summary. Recorded so they are not resurrected:
(1) benzene dimer E(C,NL) = -0.714905984299 Ha -> the file reads +0.315802583977 Ha (benz_dimer.out:799). The negative value implies dE_NLC ~ -651 kcal/mol.
(2) water dimer E(C,NL) = -0.575754 Ha -> the file reads +0.084358235133 Ha (h2o_dimer.out:674), implying -415 kcal/mol.
(3) 'the npal=1 benzene dimer did not terminate normally' -> benz_dimer.out:1504 prints ORCA TERMINATED NORMALLY.
(4) 'ref/01_h2o_orca.inp:2 proves the archived run used WB97X-V' -> that line reads '! B97 6-31G*', which has no VV10 term; the archived ωB97X-V output is ref/h2o_wb97xv.out.

Shared root cause with this morning's error: searching the strings 'nonlocal'/'nloc'/'VV10' and, finding none, concluding ORCA never separated the term. ORCA labels it 'NL Energy, E(C,NL)'. Absence of a searched string is not absence of the quantity. Second lesson: an SCF table prints E(VV10-nl) on every cycle including unconverged ones, so a printed number is not evidence a run finished - read the termination line too.
